\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput.fieldDegree}

to be $\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$, where $\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ is the least natural
number $d$ such that $2^d\geq n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Certified binary field implementation]
\lean{FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput.fieldImplementation}

For an executable Vandermonde input with output dimension $n$, let
$\ell=\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$. The field implementation assigns a certified binary
field implementation of degree $\ell$: a vector of $\ell$ low coefficients over
$\mathbb{F}_2$ whose associated monic polynomial is irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Enumerated binary cube point]
\lean{FABL.executableVandermondePoint}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p154-b007}

Let an executable Vandermonde input have output dimension $n$, and put
$\ell=\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$. For each index $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the
associated point in $\mathbb{F}_2^\ell$ is the binary-vector enumeration of the index
$j$.
\end{definition}

Let $k,n$ be positive integers with $k\le n$, and put $d=\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$.
Assign to each $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ the length-$d$ binary vector at position $j$ in an

\begin{definition}[Executable Vandermonde matrix]
\lean{FABL.executableVandermondeMatrix}
\statementsource{BGW88}{pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p004-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p154-b007}
\label{FABL.executableVandermondeMatrix}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput, FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput.fieldDegree, FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput.fieldDegree_pos, FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput.fieldImplementation, FABL.binaryPowMod, FABL.executableVandermondePoint, FABL.executableVandermondeRowEquiv, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let an executable Vandermonde input have independence order $k$ and output dimension
$n$, and put $\ell=\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$. The matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$ has
$(k-1)\ell+1$ rows and $n$ columns: its row indexed by the constant component consists
of ones, while a row indexed by $(q,i)$ has, in column $j$, the $i$th coefficient of the
reduction modulo the chosen irreducible polynomial of the $(q+1)$st power of the point
associated with $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Dimension of a binary field extension]
\lean{FABL.executableBinaryField_finrank}
\label{FABL.executableBinaryField_finrank}

\difficulty{3}
Let $\ell$ be a natural number, and let $m(X)$ be a monic polynomial of degree $\ell$
over the field with two elements, with its lower coefficients specified by a binary
vector. If $m(X)$ is irreducible, then the quotient field obtained by adjoining a root
of $m$ has dimension $\ell$ over the field with two elements.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Vandermonde field equivalence]
\lean{FABL.executableVandermondeFieldEquiv}
\label{FABL.executableVandermondeFieldEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryExtensionField, FABL.CertifiedBinaryFieldImplementation, FABL.binaryMonicPolynomial, FABL.binaryMonicPolynomial_monic, FABL.executableBinaryField_finrank, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $\ell\in\mathbb N$, and let $f(X)=X^\ell+\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}a_iX^i$ be an
irreducible polynomial over $\mathbb F_2$, with each $a_i\in\mathbb F_2$. Then the field
obtained by adjoining a root of $f$ is isomorphic to the degree-$\ell$ extension field
of $\mathbb F_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Vandermonde point in the binary extension field]
\lean{FABL.executableVandermondeFieldPoint}

Let an executable Vandermonde input have output dimension $n$, and put
$\ell=\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$. For each index $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, its
associated point in the degree-$\ell$ Galois field over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is the image,
under the field equivalence determined by the chosen irreducible polynomial, of the
encoded binary-vector point associated with $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Work for constructing Vandermonde power rows]
\lean{FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork}
\label{FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.executableSmallBiasPowerWork}
For each natural number $\ell$, define the work for constructing $p$ Vandermonde power
rows recursively by $W(0)=0$ and, for $p\ge 0$, $W(p+1)=W(p)+B(\ell,p+1)+\ell+1$, where
$B(\ell,e)$ is the work for constructing a small-bias power with parameters $\ell,e$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sum formula for power-row work]
\lean{FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork_eq_sum}
\label{FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork_eq_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.executableSmallBiasPowerWork, FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $\ell,p$, let $M(\ell)$ denote the work of one binary modular
multiplication, and define $A(\ell,e)=\ell+e(M(\ell)+1)$. Define $P_\ell(0)=0$ and
$P_\ell(p+1)=P_\ell(p)+A(\ell,p+1)+\ell+1$. Then
$P_\ell(p)=\sum_{q=0}^{p-1}(A(\ell,q+1)+\ell+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound for power-row work]
\lean{FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork_le}
\label{FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryMulModWork, FABL.executableSmallBiasPowerWork_eq, FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $\ell,p$, let $M(\ell)$ denote the work of one binary modular
multiplication, define $A(\ell,e)=\ell+e(M(\ell)+1)$, and define $P_\ell(0)=0$ and
$P_\ell(p+1)=P_\ell(p)+A(\ell,p+1)+\ell+1$. Then $P_\ell(p)\le
p\bigl(2\ell+p(M(\ell)+1)+1\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Executable Vandermonde Construction Work]
\lean{FABL.executableVandermondeConstructionWork}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p154-b008,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p155-b001
}
\label{FABL.executableVandermondeConstructionWork}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryConstructorTraversalWork, FABL.binaryFieldPreprocessingWork, FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork}
For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, set $\ell=\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$. The executable
Vandermonde construction work is the sum of the binary-field preprocessing work at
degree $\ell$ and the binary-constructor traversal work with row budget equal to the
power-row work at degree $\ell$ and exponent parameter $k-1$, plus one, on the list
$0,1,\ldots,n-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Vandermonde construction work formula]
\lean{FABL.executableVandermondeConstructionWork_eq}
\label{FABL.executableVandermondeConstructionWork_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryConstructorTraversalWork_eq, FABL.binaryFieldPreprocessingWork, FABL.executableVandermondeConstructionWork, FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, set $\ell=\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$, where
$\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ is the least natural number $r$ such that $2^r\ge n$. The work
assigned to the executable Vandermonde construction with parameters $k,n$ is the binary
field preprocessing work at parameter $\ell$, plus $n$ times one more than the work for
the first $k-1$ power rows at parameter $\ell$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vandermonde construction work as a sum]
\lean{FABL.executableVandermondeConstructionWork_eq_sum}
\label{FABL.executableVandermondeConstructionWork_eq_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryFieldPreprocessingWork, FABL.executableSmallBiasPowerWork, FABL.executableVandermondeConstructionWork, FABL.executableVandermondeConstructionWork_eq, FABL.executableVandermondePowerRowsWork_eq_sum}
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, set $\ell=\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$, with
$\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ denoting the least natural number $r$ such that $2^r\ge n$. The
executable Vandermonde construction work is the sum of the binary field preprocessing
work at parameter $\ell$ and $n$ times one plus the sum, over $q=0,\ldots,k-2$, of the
executable small-bias power work at parameter $\ell$ and exponent $q+1$, together with
$\ell+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Vandermonde input scale]
\lean{FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput.scale}
\label{FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput.scale}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput}
Let $k,n\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $1\le k\le n$. The scale of this input is $n^k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial budget]
\lean{FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput.polynomialBudget}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p154-b008}
\label{FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput.polynomialBudget}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput, FABL.ExecutableVandermondeInput.scale}
For an executable Vandermonde input with scale $s$, the polynomial budget is
$2^{17}(s+1)^8$.
\end{definition}
